explanations: luna: Earth is made a bed and the sky a canopy, then water brings out fruit. This joins the source section's soft earth to its rain-bearing sky. | terra: Allah makes earth a resting spread, sky a canopy, and sends water that brings fruit from earth; the section's sky-ground-water relation is assembled in one verse.
terra: Prayer and patience are difficult except for الْخَاشِعِينَ, locating khushu in the receptive person whose inward state governs the body.

luna: Even stones split and release water or gush out rivers; this links the source section's dry, lowered ground to the surprising emergence of flowing water. | terra: Hardened hearts are likened to stones, yet some stones gush rivers, split to release water, or fall in awe; hardness, water, opening, and lowering are held together.

luna: Among signs in the heavens and earth, rain revives dead ground; this joins the source section's sky, land, and life-after-dryness images. | terra: Rain revives earth after death, winds are turned, and cloud is held between sky and earth, assembling the section's full sky-water-soil relation.
luna: The source section's root ر ض و means contentment; this ayah joins seeking God's pleasure to a garden that bears fruit under heavy rain or light dew.
terra: A fruitful, well-watered garden is struck by a fiery whirlwind and burned when its owner is weak, reversing fertile provision into loss at the moment of need.

luna: The source section sets faces apart on that Day; this ayah divides them into faces that brighten and faces that darken, a direct contrast in facial outcomes. | terra: On the Day some faces whiten and other faces blacken; the verse uses the same face-by-face division to expose opposite outcomes.
terra: The whitened faces remain in Allah's mercy, supplying the lasting condition behind the bright half of 3:106's divided scene.
terra: A freezing wind destroys the crop of people who wrong themselves, an adverse wind-and-field scene opposite the moist wind that helps life flourish.
terra: Following Allah's رضوان is contrasted with returning under divine wrath, enacting the dictionary opposition named for ر ض و.

luna: This ayah says God is pleased with the truthful and they with Him, echoing the source section's راضية face as contentment. | terra: On the Day of truth, eternal gardens accompany Allah being pleased with the truthful and their being pleased with Him, making satisfaction reciprocal.

luna: Hardship and adversity strike earlier peoples so they might humble themselves; 6:43 supplies the same root as the source section's link from ضريع to abasement. | terra: Earlier peoples were seized with hardship and adversity so that they might humble themselves, using the ض ر ع family to connect suffering with abasement.

luna: They do not humble themselves when punishment comes and their hearts harden; the source section links ضريع's root ض ر ع with abasement. | terra: They failed to humble themselves when hardship came because their hearts hardened; hard-hearted refusal marks the boundary before compelled abasement.
terra: People call on Allah تَضَرُّعًا in the darkness and danger of land and sea, showing voluntary abasement arising from distress rather than punitive food.

luna: The ayah warns of a drink from boiling water as punishment; it is the source section's life-giving water turned into harm. | terra: Those taken by their religion as play have a drink of boiling water for their disbelief, another direct occurrence of punitive drink.
luna: Rain brings green growth, grain, dates, grapes, and other fruit from the ground; this supplies the fertile-soil side of the section's image.

luna: The source section explicitly links ضريع's root ض ر ع to humility; this ayah uses تضرعًا for humble supplication, a distinct setting of that root. | terra: The command to call on the Lord تَضَرُّعًا makes the ض ر ع family's abasement a chosen stance of prayer.

luna: Clouds are driven to a dead land, rain falls, and fruits emerge. The sequence directly fills out the section's dry-soil-to-life contrast. | terra: Winds carry heavy cloud to dead land, rain descends, and fruits emerge; sky, moist wind, water, and reviving soil meet in one scene.
terra: Good land yields growth by its Lord's leave while bad land yields only scantily; the one rain discloses two soils just as the Day discloses two kinds of face.

luna: The source section connects ضريع's root ض ر ع to abasement; here hardship is sent so a town's people may humble themselves. | terra: Towns are seized with hardship and adversity so that their people might humble themselves, repeating the punitive setting of the ضريع root's abasement sense.
luna: Hardship is replaced with prosperity in the next ayah, a specific reversal of the source section's dry and softened states.
luna: Water bursts from stone as twelve springs, a concrete spring scene matching the source section's flowing عين.
terra: Remembering the Lord inwardly with تَضَرُّعًا and fear presents the root's humble sense as sustained devotion.
terra: After gardens and lasting dwellings, رضوان from Allah is called greater; the pleasing abode does not exhaust the meaning of satisfaction.
luna: The same root ر ض و from the source section appears in mutual pleasure with God, paired here with Gardens and lasting reward.
terra: Thirst, fatigue, and hunger endured in God's path are recorded as righteous work; unlike futile exhausted labor, this نَصَب has a preserved outcome.

luna: Disbelievers receive a drink of حميم; this hot-water punishment repeats the source section's reversal of water's life-giving role. | terra: Those who disbelieve have boiling drink and painful punishment, set after the promise of just recompense for belief and good work.

luna: Rain makes the earth's growth lush before it becomes dry debris scattered by wind; the sequence links moisture, fertility, and drying. | terra: Rain mingles with earth's growth until the adorned land is suddenly reaped bare, a compressed wet flourishing and drying image for the passing life.

luna: Those who do good have no dust or humiliation on their faces, directly reversing the source section's dusted, bowed face. | terra: The doers of excellence have faces covered by neither dust nor abasement, the exact negative boundary of the dust-soiled, lowered face developed in the section.
terra: The evildoers' faces are covered by abasement and seem cut from dark night, completing 10:26's face division with the darkened counterpart.
terra: Allah raises the heavens without visible pillars and directs attention to signs, closely echoing the section's gaze toward the raised sky before 13:3 turns to earth.

luna: Earth is spread with rivers and fruits and mountains, joining the section's ground, water, and fertility details in one scene. | terra: Allah spreads the earth, places rivers in it, and grows paired fruits, completing 13:2's sky-earth pair with watered fertility.

luna: Different plots are watered by one water yet vary in produce. The source section's soft-earth dictionary sense makes this a specific contrast in land's response. | terra: Neighboring plots and gardens are watered with one water yet differ in produce; water reveals differing earth just as the Day reveals differing faces.

luna: A drink of pus follows Hell; this is water supplied as punishment, reversing the source section's expected refreshment. | terra: A defiant person has Hell ahead and is given purulent water to drink, another watering that torments rather than restores.

luna: The drink is swallowed with difficulty and barely goes down, making the burning-water reversal of the source section bodily explicit. | terra: The condemned person tries to sip the purulent water but can scarcely swallow it, showing the impossibility of relief in that drink.
terra: The faithless one's deeds are like ashes violently scattered by wind, joining lost labor to dry residue that cannot be retained.
terra: Fire covers the criminals' faces, a direct facial counterpart to dust or darkness covering faces elsewhere.
luna: Earth is spread, mountains set, and measured growth brought forth; this develops the source section's soft, fertile-ground image.
terra: Fertilizing winds are sent and water descends from the sky for people to drink; it supplies the humid-wind and sky-as-water side of the image.

luna: The God-fearing are in Gardens and springs, a direct Garden-spring parallel to the source section's عين جارية. | terra: The God-conscious are in gardens and springs; this is the setting whose couches and freedom from fatigue appear in 15:47-48.

luna: The source section's dictionary gloss for سرير connects the couch to joy without grief; here rancor is removed and people sit on facing couches. | terra: The people of the garden sit عَلَىٰ سُرُرٍ مُتَقَابِلِينَ after rancor is removed, joining the named couch to reconciled repose before fatigue is excluded.

luna: The source section names fatigue ناصبة; this ayah says no نَصَب touches the Garden's people, reversing exhausted labor. | terra: لَا يَمَسُّهُمْ فِيهَا نَصَبٌ denies fatigue in that garden, reversing the exhausted laboring condition.
luna: The sky supplies water for drinking and growth; this connects the source section's dictionary sense of samāʾ as rain to the land below.
luna: The rain of 16:10 yields grain, olives, dates, grapes, and fruit, making the section's soft, good earth visibly fertile.

luna: Water descends from the sky and revives earth after its death, the exact life-giving counterpart to the source section's dry land. | terra: Water from the sky gives earth life after death, one of the Quran's repeated direct formulations of the section's soil transformation.
terra: Whoever seeks the Hereafter and strives its proper striving in faith has a striving that is appreciated, the positive counterpart to exhausted labor.

luna: The source section's root خ ش ع evokes lowering; here people fall on their faces weeping and humility increases, a different but concrete posture. | terra: They fall upon their faces weeping and revelation increases them in خُشُوعًا; face, bodily lowering, and inward humility occur in one act.

luna: Water like molten metal burns faces; this directly reverses water's expected refreshment and brings the source section's face image into the punishment. | terra: Hell's water is like molten metal and يَشْوِي الْوُجُوهَ, directly joining a face to drink that burns instead of reviving it.
terra: The blessed recline on couches in green garments, another concrete scene of the resting object in a flourishing garden.
luna: A garden produces fruit and has a river running through it, a concrete watered-land counterpart to the source section's dry ground.

luna: A garden may be struck from the sky and become slippery barren ground; this reverses the source section's soft, fertile earth. | terra: A flourishing garden may become bare, slippery ground, showing fertile softness stripped away under judgment.

luna: Its water may sink into the earth beyond recovery, making explicit the dry-ground boundary in the source section's final sky-and-land image. | terra: Its water may sink so deep that it cannot be recovered, completing 18:40's reversal from garden to unusable ground.
luna: After the garden's water danger at 18:41, its fruit is destroyed and its trellises collapse; the ayah shows the cost of lost water.

luna: Rain produces earth's growth, then it becomes dry stubble scattered by wind; this links the section's sky, soil, and changing surface. | terra: Worldly life is rain, mingled vegetation, then dry fragments scattered by wind; softness and greenness are explicitly temporary.

luna: The source section's root ن ص ب means fatigue; Moses says the journey has brought them نَصَبًا, an ordinary travel weariness parallel to ناصبة. | terra: Moses' attendant says the journey has brought them نَصَبًا, preserving the root's plain bodily sense of fatigue from prolonged exertion.
terra: Some people's striving is lost in the nearer life while they think they act well; it explains how work can culminate in exhaustion rather than satisfaction.
terra: The Hour comes so that every soul may be recompensed for what it strives, directly joining final disclosure to سعي.

luna: Earth is made a cradle, paths are laid, and water from the sky produces varied plants; this develops the source section's ground-and-rain pairing. | terra: Allah makes earth a cradle and sends water from the sky to bring forth diverse plants, joining spread ground, watering, and fertility.

luna: The source section's root خ ش ع describes lowering and abasement; here, on the Day of Resurrection, voices are humbled before the Merciful, extending that stance beyond faces. | terra: Voices become خَشَعَتْ before the Merciful on the Day; the root shifts from face or earth to sound while keeping the sense of lowered stillness.
terra: وَعَنَتِ الْوُجُوهُ depicts all faces bowed before the Living, Self-Sustaining on the Day, a nonlexical parallel to the lowered face.
terra: The disbelievers cannot ward fire from their faces or backs, another final scene in which the face directly receives punishment.
terra: A believer's righteous effort will not be denied and is written down, the preservation that allows final satisfaction with one's striving.

luna: The source section's dictionary gloss links خاشعة with هامدة; here earth is هامدة until water makes it stir, swell, and grow, evoking resurrection. | terra: The reader sees lifeless earth, rain, stirring, swelling, and lovely growth; this is the full dry-to-soft soil process heard behind the two faces.

luna: Boiling water is poured over the heads of those in the Fire, the source section's drink turned into bodily torment. | terra: Boiling water is poured from above their heads, making destructive water descend where rain should enliven what lies below.

luna: The boiling water melts what is within them and their skins, specifying the bodily effect begun at 22:19. | terra: The boiling water melts what is in their bellies and their skins, spelling out the bodily effect of the pouring in 22:19.

luna: The ayah says God sends water from the sky until the earth turns green, a visible reversal of the section's dried, dust-covered ground. | terra: Rain descends and the earth becomes green, a concise visual change from dryness to living softness.
luna: The source section's root خ ش ع means humility; this ayah applies it to believers' prayer, a devotional rather than Judgment-Day state.

luna: Water is sent down in measure and settled in the earth; the ayah adds that God could remove it, fitting the section's question of whether land receives water. | terra: Water descends by measure and is lodged in the earth, while Allah can take it away; flowing moisture is a held provision rather than an entitlement.
luna: The settled water of 23:18 yields gardens of dates and grapes, showing the provision made possible by watered ground.

luna: Though seized by punishment, the people do not humble themselves; the ayah uses the root ض ر ع that the source section links to ضريع and abasement. | terra: Even when punishment grips them, they neither submit nor تَضَرَّعُونَ; refusal of voluntary abasement contrasts with the lowered faces of judgment.
terra: Fire scorches their faces and leaves them grimacing, another direct way punishment becomes visible on the face.
luna: The source section's dictionary sense of samāʾ includes cloud and rain; this ayah shows piled clouds, rain, and hail from the sky.
terra: Deeds are reduced to scattered dust, another concrete image of work arriving at a dry, fruitless outcome.

luna: The source section's ن ع م dictionary branch names the moist southern wind; this ayah sends winds as good tidings before pure water descends from the sky. | terra: Winds announce mercy and pure water descends from the sky, preparing the dead-land revival stated in 25:49.

luna: The ayah says rain is sent to revive a dead land and water creatures; that is the life-giving water reversed by 88:5's boiling drink. | terra: The pure water gives life to dead country and drink to creatures, uniting revived soil with the ordinary life-giving purpose of watering.
luna: The ayah asks readers to look at earth and its many good growths, matching the source section's dictionary form for soft, fertile ground.
luna: The ayah joins rain from the sky to gardens with rivers, fitting the source section's linked sky, water, and fertile-earth meanings.
terra: Those bringing evil are cast face-first into the Fire, another bodily realization of the lowered condemned face.
luna: The source section's root س ق ي means giving drink; Moses reaches water where people water their flocks, an ordinary provision scene opposite the harmful drink.
luna: Moses waters the two women's flock, then sits in shade; this completes the source section's giving-drink root in a scene of labor followed by relief.

luna: It names rain from the sky as what revives earth after death, directly joining the section's sky-and-ground images. | terra: Water from the sky revives earth after death; the repeated sign anchors the face-soil image in a general divine pattern.
terra: Allah brings living from dead and revives earth after its death, placing the soil process beside human emergence.

luna: Lightning, rain, and the revival of earth after death appear together, joining the source section's sky, water, and dry-ground images. | terra: Lightning brings fear and hope, then rain revives dead earth; the water's arrival stands between dread and mercy.

luna: Winds raise clouds and rain, after which people rejoice; the ayah stages the water-bearing sky that the source section hears in samāʾ. | terra: Winds raise and spread cloud, rain comes through it, and people rejoice when it reaches whom Allah wills; moist wind leads to joy as well as softened land.
luna: Before rain, people are in despair; the next ayah shows the earth revived. This gives the section's dry/wet difference a human response.

luna: It directs attention to earth revived after death and calls God the reviver of the dead, spelling out the resurrection meaning of the soil scene. | terra: The addressee is told to look at the effects of mercy in earth revived after death, making observation of transformed ground evidence for resurrection.
terra: A sent wind can leave crops yellow and provoke disbelief, reversing the rain-bearing wind and green earth of the preceding revival scene.
luna: Mountains anchor the earth, water descends from the sky, and good plants grow; this joins the source section's sky, ground, and fertility images.

luna: Water is driven to barren land, bringing out crops for people and animals; this is a close picture of the section's dry ground receiving water. | terra: Water is driven to barren land and crops emerge for livestock and people; provision appears from ground previously unable to grow.
terra: Their faces are turned about in the Fire while they regret disobedience, staging the condemned face inside its punishment.

luna: The source section's dictionary form for good earth ends in طيبة; this ayah describes Sheba's fertile settlement as بلدة طيبة beside its paired gardens. | terra: Sheba's sign is a good land with gardens on both sides and abundant provision, a concrete picture of fertile, favored ground.

luna: After the good land at 34:15, a flood replaces its gardens with bitter, sparse growth, showing water's provision turned into loss. | terra: Their turning away brings a flood that replaces the two gardens with bitter fruit and sparse trees, converting good watered ground into punitive provision.

luna: Wind drives clouds to a dead land; God brings out rain and revives the earth. This stages the section's rainless ground and its opposite. | terra: Winds raise cloud, Allah drives it to dead country and revives the earth; the verse also names this as the likeness of resurrection.

luna: The Garden's people say God removed their sorrow; this directly reverses the source section's dictionary sense of fatigue as grief leaving a mark. | terra: The garden people praise Allah for removing الْحَزَنَ, the grief that the section says can leave its trace as fatigue before 35:35 excludes fatigue itself.

luna: The same Garden passage says no نَصَب or weariness touches them, directly reversing the source section's exhausted labor. | terra: لَا يَمَسُّنَا فِيهَا نَصَبٌ وَلَا ... لُغُوبٌ removes both fatigue and weariness from the lasting home.
terra: Dead earth is given life and produces grain that people eat, joining resurrection, soil, and nourishing food.

luna: The source section names عين as a spring; this ayah says God made gardens and brought forth springs in the earth. | terra: Gardens are made in the revived earth and springs are caused to burst within them, adding the flowing-eye result to 36:33.
terra: The garden companions recline with their spouses on couches in shade, joining the seat to repose and shelter.
terra: The sincere servants sit on couches facing one another, preserving the couch as a social scene of untroubled joy.

luna: The source section's عين is a spring; here the righteous pass a cup of drink from a flowing spring, the life-giving counterpart to boiling water. | terra: A cup from a flowing source is passed around the garden company, contrasting communal pleasant drink with forced burning drink.
terra: The Quran asks whether garden hospitality or the tree of Zaqqum is better, setting blessed provision against punitive food before 37:66-67.
terra: The condemned eat from Zaqqum and fill their bellies, another food whose function is punishment rather than nourishment.

luna: After eating from the tree of Zaqqum, they receive a mixture of boiling water, joining failed nourishment to the source section's harmful drink. | terra: Their food is followed by a mixture of boiling water, pairing punitive eating and drinking as in the section.

luna: The source section names ن ص ب for exhaustion and grief's mark; Job describes being touched by نُصْبٍ and suffering. | terra: Job names his affliction نُصْبٍ وَعَذَابٍ, using the section's fatigue root for bodily suffering before 38:42 answers it with cool water.
terra: A cool washing place and drink relieve Job's نُصْب in 38:41; this water heals the exhausted body, the direct reverse of the boiling spring.
terra: The condemned are told to taste boiling water and foul fluid, repeating the destructive drink pair.

luna: Water is channeled as springs; crops grow, yellow, and crumble. This joins flowing water to the section's moist and dry ground states. | terra: Water descends, travels as springs in the earth, raises crops, and then the crops yellow and crumble; the verse gives the entire wet-soft-to-dry cycle.
terra: Skins and hearts soften to God's remembrance after shivering, supplying an inward softening opposite the hardened heart and dry-earth condition.
terra: A person tries to shield himself from the worst punishment with his face, making the face the exposed bearer of torment.

luna: Faces are blackened on the Day of Resurrection, another public face-boundary against the source section's fresh and softened faces. | terra: On the Day of Resurrection those who lied about Allah are seen with blackened faces, placing final moral condition on the facial surface.
terra: Allah saves the God-conscious so that evil does not touch them and they do not grieve, another final removal of marked sorrow.

luna: The punished are dragged through boiling water and then fire; it repeats the source section's reversal of water into heat. | terra: They are dragged in boiling water and then burned in the Fire, making hot water part of the punishment itself.

luna: The source section's root خ ش ع also names dry, sunken earth; here الأرض خاشعة until rain makes it stir and swell, then the ayah links revival to raising the dead. | terra: The earth itself is أَرْضَ خَاشِعَةً, then water makes it stir and swell; the verse states outright the section's transfer between a humbled dry face, watered soil, and resurrection.
luna: Rain comes after people despair and spreads mercy; the ayah links a dry, despairing state with water's relief.

luna: The source section's root خ ش ع describes abasement; here wrongdoers face the Fire خاشعين من الذل, with lowered, fearful eyes on Judgment Day. | terra: The condemned are خَاشِعِينَ مِنَ الذُّلِّ and look furtively when exposed to the Fire; khushu here is visibly the abasement heard in the face.
luna: The ayah calls earth a cradle and gives paths through it; it shares the source section's attention to the formed ground.

luna: The source section says the sky can name rain; this ayah sends measured water and revives a dead land with it. | terra: Measured water descends from the sky and revives dead country, followed by the promise that people will likewise be brought out.
terra: Couches appear among the silver furnishings that could have been universal worldly luxury, testing the assumption that the object itself guarantees blessedness.
terra: Those furnishings are only enjoyment of the nearer life, while the Hereafter with the Lord is for the God-conscious; it supplies the couch's moral boundary.
terra: The garden addressees are promised neither fear nor grief, excluding the sorrow that the section hears as leaving a mark of fatigue.

luna: The Garden's people enter with their spouses in joy, giving a concrete setting for the source section's soft face and couch named from delight. | terra: They and their spouses enter the garden delighted, supplying the joy-filled condition announced in 43:68.

luna: The tree of Zaqqum is food for the sinner, beginning a punishment passage whose drink and boiling heat mirror the source section's failed nourishment. | terra: The tree of Zaqqum is introduced as the food at the start of a food-and-boiling-water punishment sequence.

luna: The tree is food for the sinful, specifying the failed provision that precedes the hot liquid at 44:45–48. | terra: Zaqqum is called the food of the sinful, directly identifying the eater and punitive meal.

luna: The food boils in their bellies like molten metal; this is a sharp opposite to the source section's expected nourishment and refreshment. | terra: The food is like molten metal in bellies, turning ingestion into internal burning rather than nourishment.

luna: The food boils like water; this continues the heat image leading to the drink poured over them at 44:48. | terra: It boils like the boiling of scalding water, joining the punitive food's effect to the section's heated spring.

luna: Boiling water is poured over the sinner's head, a direct reversal of rain or a spring refreshing dry ground. | terra: Boiling-water punishment is poured over the sinner's head, completing the sequence begun with Zaqqum.

luna: After the hot-water punishment in this passage, the God-fearing are in Gardens and springs, a clear reversal of the source section's boiling spring. | terra: The God-conscious dwell securely among gardens and springs, repeating the garden-plus-water-eye scene.

luna: Rain and the revival of earth after death are signs, giving the source section's dry soil a stated divine-significance context. | terra: Provision descends from the sky and revives earth after death, with the turning winds named beside it as a sign.
terra: Creating heaven and earth did not weary Allah, and the verse concludes that He can give the dead life; divine action joins absence of exhaustion to resurrection.

luna: Garden rivers of unaltered water stand in the same ayah against boiling water that cuts the insides, compressing the source section's running-spring and hot-spring reversal. | terra: Paradise has water whose quality does not spoil, while the condemned drink boiling water that cuts their bowels; one verse sets life-giving and destructive drink across a boundary.
terra: They follow what angers Allah and dislike His رضوان, so their deeds are nullified; approval and wrath govern whether labor endures.
terra: The believers' distinguishing trace is visible on their faces from prostration, confirming that an inward and bodily stance can leave a readable facial mark.

luna: The section asks readers to look at the sky; this ayah likewise directs them to the sky above and how it was built. | terra: People are asked whether they have looked at the sky above them and how it was built and adorned, the same observational stance toward the raised sky.

luna: The ayah pairs the built sky with earth spread out, mountains set, and growth from the ground, matching the section's sky-and-earth gaze. | terra: The earth is spread, stabilized, and made to grow beautiful pairs, completing 50:6's sky-to-earth act of looking.
luna: The passage calls the sky and earth a reminder and insight; this adds the purpose of looking at creation in the neighboring scene at 50:6–7.

luna: The source section's dictionary sense for good earth is soft and fertile; this ayah sends blessed water from the sky and grows gardens and grain. | terra: Blessed water descends from the sky and grows gardens and harvested grain, beginning a provision scene that ends in resurrection.

luna: The same rain scene continues with tall palms and clustered fruit, showing what watered, fertile land yields. | terra: Tall date palms with layered clusters show the fresh abundance produced by the blessed water of 50:9.

luna: The rain-grown produce is provision, and the ayah says a dead land is revived; this completes the image begun at 50:9. | terra: The growth is provision, dead land is revived by water, and human emergence is likened to it; the sequence completes the image's implication.

luna: The source section's dictionary form ناصبة names exhausting labor; this ayah denies لُغُوبٍ in creation, a possible but indirect boundary with human strain. | terra: Creation of heaven and earth touched Allah with no weariness, drawing a sharp boundary between creaturely exhausted labor and the Creator's work.
terra: The God-conscious are amid gardens and springs, another concise placement of the blessed in watered ground.
luna: The source section's ن ع م dictionary branch names the moist southern wind; this ayah calls the wind sent to ʿĀd sterile (العقيم), a specific opposite.
luna: The sterile wind leaves nothing it passes without turning it to decay, completing the opposite of the source section's moist, growth-giving wind.
terra: The heaven is built with power, beginning another tightly paired statement of sky and earth.

luna: The ayah says earth was spread out, a direct scene parallel to the section's attention to how earth lies open before the observer. | terra: The earth is spread out and Allah is declared an excellent spreader, completing the cosmic pair with the same ground action as the section.
luna: The source section's root ن ع م names softness, freshness, and bliss; this ayah places the righteous in نعيم before describing their joy and couches.

luna: They rejoice in what their Lord has given and been saved from; this is the satisfaction and joy that frames the couches at 52:20. | terra: The garden people rejoice in what their Lord gives them, providing the joyful condition of those reclining on couches in 52:20.
luna: They are told to eat and drink gladly for what they did, joining reward for effort to the source section's satisfied face.

luna: The source section connects the word سرر to سرور; this ayah places the Garden's people on couches after saying they rejoice in God's gift and reward for their deeds. | terra: The blessed recline on arranged couches, another fulfillment of the resting object whose name the section relates to joy.
luna: The source section's ن ع م dictionary branch names a moist wind; the saved people say God protected them from the scorching punishment of samūm.
terra: A human being has only what he strives for; this makes the final face's relation to its own سعي accountable rather than decorative.
terra: A person's striving will be seen, the disclosure that connects present labor to the face that bears its result.
terra: The striving will receive the fullest recompense, completing the sequence that makes satisfaction with one's effort intelligible.
terra: خُشَّعًا أَبْصَارُهُمْ describes humbled eyes as people emerge from graves, locating the same lowering in the resurrection face.
terra: The earth bursts with springs and its water meets the descending water for a decreed flood, showing the water-eye as destructive excess rather than garden refreshment.
terra: The criminals are dragged on their faces into the Fire, joining bodily abasement to the punished face.
luna: Hell is the place where they denied; the next ayah says they move between it and boiling water, the source section's water turned to punishment.

luna: They circle between Fire and boiling water, exactly the burning-water boundary against the Garden spring in the source section. | terra: The condemned circulate between Hell and حَمِيمٍ آنٍ; آنٍ is the masculine form of the source section's boiling-water adjective آنيَة.

luna: The source section describes عين جارية; here two Garden springs flow, matching both the spring and its movement. | terra: The two gardens contain two flowing springs, closely matching the section's عَيْنٌ جَارِيَةٌ.
terra: The blessed recline on furnishings lined with brocade while garden fruit hangs near, placing repose inside moist abundance.

luna: Two more Garden springs gush; this repeats the source section's spring image in a second pair of Gardens. | terra: Two other gardens contain two gushing springs, preserving the water-eye while distinguishing its mode of flow.

luna: The source section's dictionary explanation connects سرير to joy; this Garden scene places its people on couches, making that word-image concrete. | terra: The foremost are on woven couches, placing the object at the center of their repose.
terra: They recline on those couches facing one another, completing the restful communal scene begun in 56:15.

luna: The Garden's people receive cups and a drink from a flowing spring, matching the source section's عين جارية and drink provision. | terra: Cups, pitchers, and a cup from a flowing source are carried among the blessed near the couches of 56:15-16.
luna: The Garden scene includes poured-out water, a flowing-water counterpart to the boiling drink and dry ground of the source section.
luna: Abundant Garden fruit follows the poured-out water of 56:31, continuing the source section's image of provision from a watered, fertile setting.

luna: Raised beds in the Garden continue the source section's elevated couches and the ease opposite to laboring, exhausted faces. | terra: Raised furnishings in the right-hand garden echo the raised couches of the section and oppose the lowered condition of the other faces.

luna: The source section's ن ع م dictionary branch names the moist southern wind; this ayah gives the punished scorching wind and boiling water, reversing that freshness. | terra: The people of the left are amid scorching wind and boiling water, joining destructive heat to a wind-and-moisture pair that reverses the section's softening climate.
luna: Their shade is black smoke, neither cool nor good; it sharpens the contrast between the source section's dry ground and fresh Garden.
luna: The shade is neither cool nor refreshing, reversing the soft, pleasant condition of the source section's Garden faces.
terra: The straying deniers eat from the tree of Zaqqum, beginning another explicit food-and-hot-water pair.
terra: They fill their bellies from that tree, emphasizing a meal that gives no wholesome nourishment.

luna: They drink boiling water after their food, matching the source section's harmful drink rather than life-giving water. | terra: They then drink boiling water upon the food, the same punitive conjunction of eating and watering.

luna: They drink like thirsty camels, continuing the hot-water punishment begun at 56:54 and the failed relief in 88:5. | terra: They drink like desperately thirsty camels, showing that the hot drink does not resolve the thirst that drives them to it.
luna: After the hot drink and the thirsty-camel comparison, this ayah calls it their welcome on the Day of Recompense, identifying the drink as punitive provision.
terra: People are asked to consider what they sow, directing the contemplative gaze to cultivated ground before its true grower is named.
terra: The question asks whether people make the crop grow or Allah does, locating fertile softness and food in divine action.
terra: Allah could make the crop dry debris, marking the boundary between nourishing growth and ruined vegetation.
terra: People are asked to consider the water they drink, shifting the same contemplative sequence from soil and crop to watering.
terra: The question asks whether people send water down from rain clouds or Allah does, explicitly tying drink to the sky.
terra: Allah could make the water bitter, defining the boundary between drink that sustains and drink that cannot refresh.
luna: For the denier, the welcome is boiling water; this repeats the source section's drink turned into torment.
luna: Burning in Hell follows the boiling-water welcome at 56:93, completing that punishment sequence.

luna: The source section's root خ ش ع means bowing; this ayah asks believers' hearts to humble at God's remembrance, extending the same inward posture. | terra: Hearts are asked to become تَخْشَعَ and are warned against hardening; the inner softness behind bodily khushu is set beside the revived earth in 57:17.

luna: The ayah explicitly says God gives life to earth after its death, making the source section's dry land a sign of resurrection. | terra: Allah gives the earth life after its death; following 57:16, the soil's softening interprets how a hardened heart can become humble.

luna: Rain-fed growth eventually yellows and becomes debris, extending the section's contrast between freshness and dryness to the life of plants. | terra: Rain-fed growth delights its cultivators, then dries, yellows, and becomes debris; the soft fresh condition is set within its earthly limit.

luna: The source section defines ر ض و through the opposite of displeasure; this ayah uses mutual pleasure with God as the believers' outcome. | terra: Gardens and mutual satisfaction between Allah and the faithful make رضى the final relation of an enduring community.

luna: The source section's root خ ش ع names a low, bowed condition; here a mountain would become humbled and split from fear of God. | terra: A mountain would become خَاشِعًا and split from fear of Allah; even a hard raised body can be lowered and broken open.
terra: When the promised punishment is seen close at hand, the disbelievers' faces become distressed; encounter turns inward dread into a visible face.

luna: If water sinks into the earth, who can bring a flowing spring? This names the boundary between the section's dry face and its running-water garden. | terra: If water sinks away, no one can bring flowing water; it marks the boundary between a land with an accessible spring and one deprived of it.

luna: The source section's root خ ش ع describes a lowered face; here eyes are humbled and disgrace covers them on the promised Day. | terra: خَاشِعَةً أَبْصَارُهُمْ and covering abasement join lowered eyes to the humiliation that the section's dry face bears.

luna: The source section has راضية for being content with one's effort; this ayah describes the good outcome as عيشة راضية. | terra: فِي عِيشَةٍ رَاضِيَةٍ uses the same رضو root for a pleasing life after the record is received, extending satisfaction from effort to its abode.
luna: They eat and drink in satisfaction for what they did before, making explicit the effort-and-reward relation in the source section.
terra: وَلَا طَعَامٌ إِلَّا مِنْ غِسْلِينٍ repeats the exclusive 'no food except' construction of the ضريع verse with another punitive food.
terra: Only sinners eat the غسلين of 69:36; the verse fixes the eater and punitive function of that exclusive food.

luna: Eyes are خاشعة on the Day of Judgment, repeating the source section's root خ ش ع in an eschatological facial expression. | terra: خَاشِعَةً أَبْصَارُهُمْ and enveloping abasement describe the promised Day, repeating the humbled-eye face scene.
luna: The ayah says God made earth a spread-out expanse, repeating the ground-forming scene that the section asks readers to observe.
terra: The threatened judgment contains choking food and painful punishment, another food whose physical quality torments instead of nourishing.

luna: Some faces are fresh on that day, directly answering the source section's pair of humbled and soft, fresh faces. | terra: وُجُوهٌ يَوْمَئِذٍ نَاضِرَةٌ gives the same Day-of-Judgment subject and makes freshness visible directly on the face.

luna: The fresh faces of 75:22 look toward their Lord; this adds their stance to the positive face-state parallel. | terra: The fresh faces of 75:22 are looking toward their Lord; this verse supplies the object and fulfillment of their freshness.

luna: Other faces are grim on that day, the negative face-state paired against 88:8's freshness and the source section's softened face. | terra: وَوُجُوهٌ يَوْمَئِذٍ بَاسِرَةٌ places the scowling face opposite the fresh face of 75:22, matching the section's paired openings.

luna: The grim faces of 75:24 expect a crushing disaster, explaining the negative face-state that contrasts with the source section's freshness. | terra: The scowling faces of 75:24 expect a crushing calamity; this verse supplies the apprehension embodied in their expression.
luna: The righteous are given a drink blended with camphor, a cool Garden counterpart to the boiling drink in the source section.

luna: The source section defines عين as a spring; here the servants drink from a spring they cause to gush, opposite the boiling source at 88:5. | terra: The righteous drink from a spring whose flow they cause to gush abundantly; the spring is both drink and freely running source.

luna: The source section says سرير is named from سرور and describes sorrow-free joy; this ayah joins freshness نضرة with joy سرور. | terra: Allah meets the patient with نَضْرَةً وَسُرُورًا, joining fresh appearance to the joy from which the section hears the couch's name and reversing marked grief.
luna: The Garden reward follows patient labor, matching the source section's contrast between exhausted work and contentment with one's effort.

luna: The Garden has no scorching sun or bitter cold; this gives the fresh faces and pure drink of 76:11–12 a climate opposite to torment. | terra: The rewarded recline on couches and experience neither sun nor bitter cold, giving the seat a temperate, restful environment.
luna: A Garden drink is blended with ginger, continuing the pleasant drink opposite the source section's hot water.

luna: The source section's عين is a flowing spring; this ayah names a Garden spring, Salsabil, as a drink. | terra: A spring in the garden is named Salsabil, continuing the blessed drink sequence as the counterpart of the boiling spring.

luna: God gives the Garden's people a pure drink, the life-giving counterpart to the boiling water served in the source section. | terra: The blessed are given a pure drink by their Lord, completing the same passage's fresh face, joy, couch, and spring with life-giving watering.
terra: كَانَ سَعْيُكُمْ مَشْكُورًا tells the blessed that their striving is appreciated, stating why a face can be satisfied with its effort.

luna: The God-fearing are in shade and springs, matching the source section's Garden spring as relief from hot, dry punishment. | terra: The God-conscious are amid shades and springs, joining shelter and available water in the final abode.

luna: Earth is made a resting spread, matching the source section's dictionary image of low, ground-hugging earth. | terra: The earth is made a resting spread, another direct formulation of the ground laid out for creaturely life.
luna: Mountains are set as pegs after earth is spread; this continues the formed-land scene that the source section pairs with sky and earth.
luna: The seven heavens are built above the spread earth and pegged mountains, continuing the same sky-and-ground arrangement.
luna: Clouds pour abundant water, giving the sky in the source section its dictionary sense of rain. | terra: Abundant water is poured from rain clouds, beginning a compact sky-to-earth sequence.

luna: The rain of 78:14 brings grain and plants from the ground, showing what water does to earth. | terra: The poured water brings forth grain and vegetation, showing its nourishing rather than burning effect.

luna: The same rain sequence ends in thick gardens, completing the connection between the source section's sky and fertile ground. | terra: Dense gardens are the mature result of the water and growth in 78:14-15.

luna: In Hell they taste neither coolness nor drink, a direct boundary against the source section's soft, moist Garden. | terra: In Hell they taste neither coolness nor drink, denying precisely what parched soil or a weary body needs before 78:25 names the substitute.

luna: The only drink is boiling water and foul fluid, making explicit the source section's reversal of water. | terra: إِلَّا حَمِيمًا وَغَسَّاقًا replaces cool drink with boiling water and foul fluid, closely matching the section's reversed watering.
luna: The boiling drink is requital, giving the hot-water scene at 78:25 its stated relation to deeds.

luna: The source section's root خ ش ع means bowing and abasement; here eyes are خاشعة on the Day, matching the humbled-face state. | terra: أَبْصَارُهَا خَاشِعَةٌ places khushu in the eyes of hearts terrified by resurrection, another bodily location of the lowered face.

luna: The ayah asks who built the sky; the passage then turns to earth, water, pasture, and mountains, echoing the source section's gaze upward and down. | terra: The question whether humanity or heaven is harder to create introduces the construction of the sky whose paired earth and water appear in 79:30-31.

luna: After the sky, earth is spread out; 79:31 names its water and pasture, completing a land-and-rain scene related to the source section. | terra: The earth is spread after the sky is built, matching the section's paired invitation to look at sky and laid-out ground.

luna: Earth's water and pasture are brought forth, matching the source section's dictionary meanings of rain-bearing sky and good ground. | terra: Water and pasture are brought out from that earth, showing what the spread ground holds when made life-bearing.
luna: Mountains are set after earth's water and pasture; this continues the same created landscape considered by the source section.
luna: The water, pasture, and mountains serve people and their livestock, completing the passage's account of the land's provision.
terra: On the Day a person remembers what he strove for, making the remembered effort part of the judgment scene.
terra: The one who feared standing before his Lord and restrained desire supplies the action behind the favorable outcome in 79:41.
terra: The garden is the refuge of the person described in 79:40, completing an effort-to-abode sequence parallel to the satisfied face.

luna: Rain is poured down abundantly, then the earth is split open; the following verses show the fertile growth of the source section's soft earth. | terra: Water is poured abundantly, opening another Quranic soil sequence just before the same surah's two kinds of face.

luna: The ground opens after rain, making visible the soil's response that stands opposite the source section's dry land. | terra: The earth is split open, the receptive action by which the water of 80:25 becomes growth.

luna: Grain comes from the opened earth, a concrete result of the rain-and-soil scene begun at 80:25. | terra: Grain is caused to grow in the opened, watered earth, distinguishing nourishing water from the punitive drink.
luna: Grapes grow from the watered earth, continuing the produce list that makes fertile ground visible.
luna: Olives and palms continue the crops produced after rain, extending the source section's image of ground made fit by water.
luna: Dense gardens complete the rain-grown landscape begun at 80:25, the opposite of dry, dusty earth.
luna: Fruit and pasture continue the yield of the opened earth, showing its provision after rain.
luna: The produce is provision for people and livestock, completing the rain-to-food sequence begun at 80:25.

luna: The deafening cry marks the Day when the dusty faces of 80:40 appear; the cited verse supplies that scene's onset, not its dust. | terra: The deafening blast announces the moment at which the opposed faces of 80:38-42 appear; its own contribution is the event that changes the scene.

luna: Some faces are bright in the same passage where others are dusty; this supplies a direct face-to-face contrast for the source image. | terra: Faces that Day are bright; this is the luminous half of the face pair whose dusty half appears in 80:40.

luna: The bright faces laugh and rejoice, while the passage's other faces are dusty and gloomy; this clarifies the two outcomes in the source section. | terra: Those bright faces are laughing and rejoicing, giving the inward joy corresponding to the section's soft, happy face.

luna: Dust lies on faces in the same reckoning scene as the bright, laughing faces just before; this joins dusty earth and dusty faces as in the source section. | terra: وُجُوهٌ يَوْمَئِذٍ عَلَيْهَا غَبَرَةٌ joins a face and settled dust explicitly, making the commentary's dusty-land hearing visible.

luna: Gloom covers faces next to the dust-covered faces of 80:40, continuing the source section's image of a crushed, dusty face. | terra: Darkness overspreads the dust-covered faces of 80:40, showing that the dust is a condition of the whole face rather than a stray detail.

luna: The passage identifies the dusty, gloomy faces just described as disbelievers and sinners, adding the moral outcome to that scene. | terra: The dusty, darkened faces belong to the faithless and shameless; the verse identifies the moral outcome embodied in 80:40-41.

luna: The source section's root ن ع م names softness and bliss; the righteous are in نعيم in the passage that shows couches, fresh faces, and a spring. | terra: The righteous are in نعيم, the condition whose freshness becomes readable on their faces in 83:24.

luna: They recline on couches in the passage that describes fresh faces and a spring, bringing the source section's couch and face images together. | terra: They look out from couches, linking restful seating to the face whose radiance is identified in the following verse.

luna: The source section links ناعمة to freshness and نعمة; this ayah says bliss's freshness is recognizable on faces, a direct positive counterpart. | terra: نَضْرَةَ النَّعِيمِ is recognizable on the blessed faces; the نعيم family itself supplies the freshness carried by ناعمة.

luna: A sealed drink follows the fresh faces of 83:24 and precedes Tasnim's spring, echoing the source section's joined face-and-drink contrast. | terra: The people whose faces show bliss are given sealed nectar to drink, connecting visible freshness to its garden drink.
luna: The passage invites people to compete for this reward; this gives a specific effort-and-recompense parallel to the source section's satisfied face.

luna: The Garden drink is mixed with Tasnim, leading into the spring named in 83:28 and extending the source section's running-water image. | terra: Their nectar is mixed with Tasnim, preparing the identification of Tasnim as a spring in 83:28.

luna: The source section names عين as a spring; this ayah says the near ones drink from a spring, extending the fresh-face scene at 83:24. | terra: Tasnim is a spring from which those brought near drink, adding a water-eye to the couch, drink, and fresh-face cluster of 83:22-25.
terra: The righteous look out from couches, repeating the posture of 83:23 after the fate of the sinners has been disclosed.
terra: Humanity is laboring painfully toward its Lord and will meet Him; this gathers work, weariness, return, and encounter into one line.
terra: Receiving the record in the right hand begins the favorable outcome of the labor named in 84:6.

luna: The one given the record in the right hand receives an easy reckoning, the effort-and-outcome setting continued by rejoicing in 84:9. | terra: An easy accounting explains how the laborer's meeting in 84:6 leads toward joy rather than exhausted abasement.

luna: The one given the record in the right hand returns to family rejoicing, a specific outcome parallel to being content with one's effort. | terra: The one easily accounted returns مَسْرُورًا, the same joy root used to explain the couch's name and the end of grief.
luna: The source section's dictionary gloss allows samāʾ to mean rain; this oath names the sky as returning rain, paired with fissured earth in 86:12.
luna: The oath names earth with fissures, a ground image paired with returning rain at 86:11 and apt for water opening dry soil.
terra: Allah brings out pasture, the fresh phase of the earth image before its reversal in 87:5.
terra: The pasture becomes dark stubble, reversing softness and freshness into the dried residue of earthly growth.

luna: The source section's root ر ض و means the opposite of displeasure; this ayah repeats راضية مرضية for the soul welcomed into its Garden. | terra: The soul returns رَاضِيَةً مَرْضِيَّةً, both satisfied and approved, clarifying the two directions that رضى can take at the return.
luna: The contented soul of 89:28 is told to enter among God's servants, continuing the source section's movement from satisfaction to Garden ease.
luna: The contented soul is finally told to enter the Garden, completing the same contentment-to-rest movement as 88:8–10.
terra: The oath by the sky and the One who built it begins a sky-earth pair parallel to the section's paired objects of contemplation.

luna: The oath names earth and the One who spread it; this is another direct formulation of the section's spread-earth image. | terra: The oath by the earth and the One who spread it completes 91:5's pair and repeats the section's laid-out ground.
terra: إِنَّ سَعْيَكُمْ لَشَتَّىٰ states that human striving diverges, the premise for labor ending in opposed conditions.
terra: The giver who confirms the best is eased toward ease, an outcome of striving that can culminate in satisfaction rather than exhaustion.
terra: The withholding denier is eased toward hardship, the opposed course through which striving culminates in distress.
terra: After giving to be purified and seeking his Lord's face, the servant وَلَسَوْفَ يَرْضَىٰ; future satisfaction is tied to prior action.
terra: The Lord promises to give until the addressee is satisfied, presenting رضى as the response to a future divine gift rather than to one's own labor.

luna: The source section's root ر ض و names contentment; this ayah says God is pleased with them and they are pleased with Him in Gardens. | terra: Eternal gardens culminate in Allah being pleased with the faithful and their being pleased with Him, another final mutual satisfaction.
terra: فِي عِيشَةٍ رَاضِيَةٍ again makes the final life itself pleasing after the weighing of deeds.
terra: Feeding that relieves hunger states food's ordinary merciful function, the direct boundary illuminated when punitive food neither nourishes nor avails against hunger.
